voice: A calm, confident woman in her thirties with a warm, clear, mid-range voice. Neutral American English. Measured, unhurried pace with crisp articulation. Friendly and precise, like a senior engineer giving a product walkthrough. Studio quality, close microphone, no background noise.
reference: Hi, I'm going to walk you through the portal, one screen at a time, and show you what each part does.

lines.text: This is the QuickSight Assets Portal. An open source control plane for Amazon QuickSight, that runs in your own AWS account.
Every dashboard is listed with who actually opens it. Sort by activity, and see the views and the viewers behind any count.
Need to move a dataset to a new data source? Pick the source, check the preview, and apply.
The full definition of any asset is one click away, as JSON.
Select what nobody opens, and delete it. The portal archives each definition first, so nothing is lost.
The activity timeline shows who changed what, from the console, the portal, or an agent, with the stored event behind each line.
The data catalog traces every calculated field, from its source columns to the visuals that read it.
The assistant drafts a plan, and a preview of what it would build. Nothing is written until you run it.
And here is how the portal compares with AWS today, capability by capability, with the gaps on both sides.
The QuickSight Assets Portal. Open source, and one command to deploy. Everything you just saw is the real portal, running on made up data.
